content:
Quick start

nfprogress does not store the text of the manuscript, but its measurable progress. The basic unit of work is the project; A large project can be broken down into stages.

  1. Open “Projects” and click “Create Project”.
  2. Indicate the name, final goal, value already achieved and unit of measurement. If necessary, select a deadline, daily goal, stages and streaks.
  3. Select a project from the list. In the “New Entry” field, enter new general meaning, not the number written since the last entry. The application will calculate the difference itself.
  4. Keep track of your progress, your cumulative goal for today, and your recording history. In Tauri desktop, a project can be linked to local Word or Scrivener; Web and mobile versions accept an explicitly selected Word .docx file.
  5. Game mode is enabled separately in the settings. It adds rewards, character, store, quests and Creative Rhythm, but does not change project data.

Important: the daily project goal and the game goal of the day in “Creative Rhythm” are different mechanisms. The first helps to meet the deadline and supports the streak; the second is a daily challenge for an in-game reward.
title: Quick start

children.content:
List, search and navigation

  • Click a project or stage to open its details and entries. Right-clicking shows only available actions: edit, archive, delete, complete, and synchronize.
  • Select “Manual order” to rearrange projects by dragging. Hover over a card’s top-right corner and drag the handle that appears; changes are saved immediately.
  • The “New folder” button creates a folder for organizing projects. To move a project into or out of a folder, drag the handle in the card’s top-right corner or select a folder from the right-click context menu; deleting a folder does not delete its projects.
  • Search finds both projects and stages. Double-clicking a found stage clears the search, expands its parent project, and selects the stage in the regular list.
  • The filter switches between active, archived, and completed projects. Stages are shown with their parent.
  • Deadline sorting places projects without a deadline separately; progress sorting uses the overall completion percentage. The selected filter, sorting, and manual order are saved between launches.

The last selected project or stage is remembered and opened at the next launch.
children.title: List, Search, and Navigation

children.content:
Creating a Project

  1. Click New Project on the projects tab or select Project → New Project.
  2. Enter a unique, non-empty name.
  3. Specify a positive total goal and a non-negative running quantity. This allows you to start tracking the text you've already written.
  4. Select a unit: symbols, A4 sheets, author sheets or Fikbook pages. For calculations, the following ratios are used: 1 A4 sheet = 1,800 characters, 1 author’s sheet = 40,000 characters, 1 Fikbook page = 4,500 characters.
  5. Specify a deadline or check “No”. The date cannot be earlier than the current writer's day.
  6. Enable Streaks in the settings, and in the create a project or source form, leave Track Streaks enabled (this is the default setting). Auto-freezing is available in game mode.
  7. To break up the work, enable "project with sources" and add sources before saving or after creating the project.

The deadline and the Daily Goal field are related: changing one recalculates the other. Before saving, the form shows the first error found.
children.title: Creating a Project

children.content:
Project sources

Source is a nested entity with its own name, goal, current value, records, deadline, daily plan, streak and synchronization. All sources use the unit of measure of the parent project.

  • Create a source using the “Add source” button in the project form or using the “Project → Create source” item after selecting a project with sources.
  • The total goal and volume of the parent are equal to the sum of the goals and volumes of the sources; The parent's fields become read-only.
  • If a parent does not have a deadline, their displayed goal for today is the sum of the sources' daily goals. If the parent has a deadline, the total plan is calculated for the sum of the sources.
  • When adding a deadline to a parent, the longest source streak is transferred to the project, and the source streaks are cleared. Their deadlines remain the same.
  • Converting a regular project to a sourced project transfers the history, progress, project text, and synchronization to the first source. The inverse transformation combines records over time and recalculates a single progress.
  • The source cannot be archived separately, but it can be modified, completed, or deleted. Completing the entire project also completes all unfinished sources.
  • A source's actions are opened by right-clicking on its tile. Synchronization is shown only for a source with a binding configured.

In the "Common Project", sources operate as independent synchronization bindings and have infinite targets. Add a source using the “Add source” button: it is offered the name “Source N”, and after creation, select “Connect source” to configure the file. When adding a second source, the previous binding and history are preserved in “Source 1”. A source can be removed from its card or page; along with it, its binding and progress history are deleted.
children.title: Project sources

children.content:
Maps of projects and sources

Every project and every source has an idea map. The Maps section shows project tiles. The map can be opened in a section or a separate window; the selected path and viewing mode are remembered. When opened for the first time, the root node will have the name of the project or source.

  • Double-click the node or press Space to change the text. Tab adds a child node, Enter adds an adjacent node, Delete deletes the selected node.
  • “Free node” is a first-level node outside the automatic layout; his kids look like second tier. It has shortcuts, menus, links and “Description”. Using the menu or dragging, you can detach a regular branch with all children or attach a free one to a map node. Note supports editing, deleting, links and Tab to new note nearby.
  • Nodes can be dragged. The context menu adds, links, moves, and groups nodes, and the built-in panel controls zoom and centering.
  • The focus mode button on the bottom panel shows the selected first level branch separately. Pressing again returns the shared map.
  • The search icon in the top bar or Ctrl+F (Command+F on macOS) searches regular and free nodes and notes. Select a result to expand the branch you want, highlighting the item, and displaying it in the center of the map.
  • Changes are saved automatically along with the project data. The “Save” button and closing the window also records the current state of the card.
  • The Export button saves the current map as PNG, SVG or JSON. PNG and SVG are suitable for viewing and sharing, while JSON stores the editable map structure.
  • In the Edit Project with Sources window, you can enable “Merge source maps into a project map.” Then each source is shown in the general map as a separate first-level branch under its current name.
  • The contents of branches are synchronized in both directions: changes in the shared map are saved in individual source maps, and changes in an individual map appear the next time the shared map is opened. The project's own nodes are retained.
  • Renaming, adding, deleting and reordering sources are automatically reflected in the overall map. Disabling merge only hides merged branches and does not remove source maps.
  • A completed source is marked in the general map with a ✅ icon. Its existing map and branch in the shared map are view-only. If a source map has not been created, the “Map” button displays a message, and in a general map the same explanation is displayed in the bottom status line, not as a separate node. A map of the completed project is also available for viewing only.
  • When you delete a project or source, its map is also deleted. When converting a project with sources to a regular project, the maps of the deleted sources are not merged with the parent map.

The map editor works without an Internet connection.
children.title: Maps of projects and sources

children.content:
Project Notes

The Notes section in the left pane shows tiles for all projects. Notes can be opened within a section or in a separate window; The last opened project, tab and search query are remembered. The workspace contains the normal notes of the selected entity and the floating notes of its mind map.

  • “New Note” opens the editor with the cursor in the text; a new map node is not created. Clicking on the card opens the same editor. Changes are saved automatically, closing with the “Done” button, Escape or clicking on the background.
  • The title is optional. The color covers the entire editor. "Done" is on the same page as palette, archive, and delete; a filled pin means pinning.
  • Standard Ctrl/⌘ combinations work. For a link, select the text and enter the address: the correct address is saved. Tags are entered separated by commas and filter cards.
  • In the parent project, the Source Notes button separately includes cards for all sources. Each of them has a noticeable “Source: …” mark. The adjacent menu selects a single source, and the By Source switch groups the order of cards by source.
  • The search takes into account the title, text, checklist items, tags and source name. While “Source Notes” is turned off, the search only works on the notes of the project itself; once enabled, it covers sources as well. The tags menu allows you to quickly filter cards; system tag #карта only shows Mind Map notes.
  • Card #карта associated with the Mind Elixir stable element identifier. Changing its text changes the same note on the map, and creating, editing or deleting it on the map is immediately reflected among the cards.
  • System tag #карта cannot be deleted. Text formatting is not available for this card because Mind Elixir's native format stores the note as plain text. An individual card title can be changed; this does not change the name of the card element.
  • The Open on Map action opens the map, selects the associated note, and displays it in the center. Removing a card #карта requires confirmation and only deletes the associated note, not other map nodes.
  • The archive hides the card from the main list without deleting it; The “Archive” switch shows and allows you to restore such notes. Cards are arranged in order of addition in a responsive grid. Dragging the special handle changes the order, and after releasing the card always occupies a grid cell.

The note editor and grid library are included in the application and do not require an Internet connection. In a completed project or source, notes are viewable only; The same restriction applies to cards of completed sources in the general window of the parent project.
children.title: Project Notes

children.content:
Progress and records

In the New Entry field, enter the current total quantity in the selected unit. For example, if there were 12,000 characters and now there are 13,500, enter 13,500: the entry will save the change +1,500.

  • Click Save or Enter. The same value as the previous one does not create a record.
  • The increase creates a positive entry; decrease is negative. The project percentage is calculated as the current quantity divided by the goal.
  • Game rewards and character challenges are promoted only by positive difference. An active session with the intent "Edit text" also takes into account the reduction of text by modulo change.
  • The history shows the date and time, change, new total value and contribution to the project percentage. A project with sources has the source name next to it.
  • Deleting a local entry is irreversible. The total then comes from the last remaining entry, or becomes zero for an empty history. For published cloud history, deletion and correction use cloud settings with explicit rebasing of later dependent actions; original events remain preserved.

Synchronization creates the same records automatically. The start time of the writing day from the settings determines which day the early entry belongs to.
children.title: Progress and Records

children.content:
Deadlines and daily goals

The deadline is included in the calculation as a full-time working day. The remaining volume is divided by the number of days from today to the deadline inclusive. In the form, you can change the date and get a new daily rate, or change the rate and get a new date.

The card shows savings goal for today: how much should be in the project by the end of the current writing day. To find out the amount of work remaining for today, compare this mark with the current amount. The missed volume does not disappear - the next cumulative mark continues the plan.

  • When a deadline is reached or passed, the cumulative goal becomes equal to the full project goal.
  • Changing the goal, deadline, unit, sources, or personal daily rate restructures the future plan, preserving past days and taking into account what has already been written today.
  • In the change project or source window, you can check “Recalculate daily goals from today” as long as the daily goal does not change. Then today’s plan will start from the current progress, and the deadline will move along the remaining volume.
  • Removing a deadline resets the daily goal. When a streak is active, the application will warn you about its loss.
  • When streaks are enabled, you cannot reduce the daily goal before completing the current one. Increasing an already completed goal may require extending today's streak again; A repeat game reward for the same day will not be issued.

“Start time of day” in the settings shifts the border of the day. For example, if you start at 04:00, the entry at 02:00 refers to the previous writing day.
children.title: Deadlines and daily goal

children.content:
Streaks and frosts

Enable Streaks in the settings, then in the create or edit project/source form, leave Track Streaks enabled. For new entities, the checkbox is enabled by default; old entities with the local flag cleared are connected when the general setting is re-enabled. A local streak begins or extends when the current quantity reaches that day's cumulative goal.

  • The global streak is extended if the daily goal is met in at least one active streak source.
  • Statuses show whether the streak has started, was renewed today, is awaiting renewal, frozen, lost or completed along with the project.
  • In the new interface, the global streak is located above the list of projects. The project's streak is shown when the parent's deadline; if the parent does not have a deadline, own streaks are shown on the tiles of sources with deadlines and inside the open source.
  • The Freeze item covers one missed day of a suitable local or global streak. Autofreeze uses the item automatically if the condition has not yet been met and freezing is allowed.
  • Archiving a project removes its deadline and interrupts the streak. Disabling an entity's streak clears its current streak.
  • Disabling the general Streaks setting clears local and global streaks in all projects and sources.

In game mode, starting, continuing and completing streaks provide rewards. Losing a global streak causes damage to the character; successfully applied freezing prevents this loss.
children.title: Streaks and Freezes

children.content:
Sync with Word and Scrivener

In Tauri desktop, set up local source in the "Word and Scrivener" section. Subsequently, the application reads the new number of characters, compares it with the current progress and creates a record with the difference. Web, iOS and Android do not get arbitrary persistent access to the file system: there, select and download the .docx file explicitly.

  • Word: select the .docx file. The old .doc format is not supported - save the document as .docx. The text of paragraphs and tables is counted.
  • The built-in editor and linked .docx files use Arial, Georgia, Times New Roman and Courier New; sizes are specified in Word points. It preserves the main paragraph and character formats: headings, lists, blockquotes, alignment, line spacing, font styles, underline, strikethrough, superscript and subscript, tabs, text color and highlighting. Tables, images and links are unavailable in the editor so that exchange with Word remains predictable.
  • For each project and source, the built-in editor separately remembers the cursor position, scrolling, zoom, and typewriter mode state. The next time it opens, it returns to the same place with the same view settings.
  • The typewriter button to the left of the zoom controls enables typewriter mode: while typing, a line below the middle of the editor stays approximately centered. Only visual empty space is added after the document end; it is not saved in the text or exported to Word.
  • Scrivener: Only in Tauri desktop, select the local .scriv project, then a specific text document, chapter or scene. Remote and mobile clients do not upload the Scrivener project to the server.
  • For active desktop bindings, launching the selected source and synchronizing all sources are available; background synchronization only works when the desktop setting is enabled.
  • Decreasing the outer text creates a negative entry. There is no in-game reward given for it.
  • For a project with stages, each stage has its own binding, and synchronizing the parent sequentially updates all active linked stages.
  • “Delete synchronization” removes the link, but saves the already created entries and progress.

For direct synchronization, the ramp time and source stability are checked. If a file, folder, or Scrivener item is inaccessible, out of date, corrupted, or changed during reading, a new entry is not created and the binding is retained. Choose a new path or unbind manually when you really need it.
children.title: Synchronization

children.content:
Statistics and publication of progress

After selecting a project, open its statistics. It is calculated from the saved history: number of records, total volume, average values ​​for active days and records, used freezes, best day and day of the week, current and maximum streaks, duration of work and other indicators.

For a project with sources, statistics are built based on the combined chronology of all sources.

The Share button on the target project or source creates a 1080×1080 square PNG card with the title and current percentage. If a project has a cover, the card follows the look of its project card and contains the nfprogress logo. For a source, both the project and the source are listed in the title.

The Share menu contains separate actions: the copy icon writes the card to the clipboard, and the save icon starts downloading the PNG. If the clipboard is not available, the application does not automatically replace the download action; manuscript text, notes and other data are not sent to an external service.

For the infinite "General Project" and its sources, the card is not available because they do not have an end goal and percentage of completion.
children.title: Statistics and Publishing

children.content:
Modification, archiving, completion and deletion

  • Edit: allows you to update the name, goal, current value, unit, deadline, daily goal, streak and source structure. Changing units permanently converts goals, entries, and progress, with rounding provided.
  • To the archive: Available only to the top-level project. The deadline is deleted, the streak is interrupted, and the project goes into the “Archive” filter. It can be activated again, but the deadline will have to be set again.
  • Complete: available after reaching the final goal. The action is irreversible; a completed entity can be viewed or deleted, but cannot continue to be edited. Completion of the parent terminates unterminated sources.
  • Delete: permanently deletes the project or the selected source along with its history. If the last source is deleted, the parent becomes a regular project.

Game rewards for completion are given once. The source's reward is a quarter of the reward for an independent project of the same size.
children.title: Editing and Statuses

content:
Projects and sources

The project combines a goal, current volume, progress records, deadline, daily plan, status and, with streak mode enabled, its own series of productive days.

A typical project is tracked as a whole. A project with sources serves as a container: its purpose, scope and progress are compiled from the sources, and the entries are shown in a general chronology with the names of the sources.

Three statuses are available for work: active, archived and completed. The filter above the list determines which status is shown; sorting arranges projects automatically or maintains a loose order defined by drag-and-drop.
title: Projects and sources

content:
Application Settings

  • Endless Project: creates a “General Project” without an end goal. It is suitable for small unrelated texts and multiple synchronization sources. Disabling the setting deletes the “Shared Project” along with the data accumulated in it, but first creates a backup copy of the data files and settings in the folder backups.
  • Game mode: Shows or hides the game tab. Hiding does not reset a saved character.
  • Streaks: includes a global mechanism and allows you to customize project streaks. Disabling clears the history of current local and global streaks; A backup copy is also created before such a reset.
  • Show how much has been written today: displays the total result of the current writing day for all projects. In the new interface, this card is located above the list of projects.
  • Notification display time: sets how long pop-up messages remain visible; the valid range is 1 to 3,600 seconds. Saved bank and streak events can be opened with the “Notifications” button, remain in history, and are marked as read individually.
  • Start time of day: defines the writing day boundary for entries, daily goals, and streaks.
  • Language: immediately switches between Russian, English, Spanish, German, French or Brazilian Portuguese interface.
  • Interface animation: Full animation makes changes to pie charts and progress bars noticeable; Same as System mode follows the operating system's motion reduction setting, and Reduced turns off decorative motion.
  • Check for updates: available in the official desktop version. The application also checks for new versions after startup and once an hour. Every package must pass digital-signature verification before installation; local test builds are not connected to the update channel.

Settings are available in the separate “Settings” section.
title: Application Settings

content:
Developer Mode

Available only in the local development runtime, test build, or explicitly allowed developer profile. A separate window allows you to change the test date and character parameters and issue items without the usual store limits.

Replacing real/test profile is performed only upon explicit request after a restart. Before atomic activation, a backup copy is created and verified. Persistent test profile is not automatically updated.
title: Developer Mode

children.content:
Rewards, levels and health

  • Basically, every 100 added symbols give 10 coins and 500 experience. The total is multiplied by the character's parameters, inspiration, effects, specialization and relics.
  • Negative entries do not take away previously issued rewards, but also do not give new ones.
  • When leveling up, the character receives coins, fully restores health, and receives 2 skill points per new level.
  • Maximum health starts at 100 and increases by 10 every five levels.
  • Prices and some cash rewards take inflation into account: its multiplier increases by 15% for each level after the first.
  • Starting, extending and completing streaks provide separate rewards. Losing a global streak causes 5 damage for each streak day lost.
  • At zero health, the existing resurrection potion is automatically used or you are offered to buy it. Without resurrection, the character returns to level 1, loses all experience and inventory and half the coins.

Completing a project provides a one-time reward based on volume; source completion uses a factor of 25%.
children.title: Rewards, levels, and health

children.content:
Character parameters and skills

On the parameters tab, coin, experience, and health recovery multipliers are shown. Select a row to see the actual effect of the multiplier considering level, skills, and active items.

  • Productivity adds +0.25 to the experience multiplier for each invested point.
  • Profitability adds +0.25 to the coin multiplier per point.
  • Endurance restores an additional 0.25 health per hour per point.

2 points are awarded for each new level. Increase the value of the desired skill with the counter; confirmed points cannot be removed or transferred to another skill.

Temporary buffs, debuffs, and permanent item effects are added on top of the base multipliers. Lists show the parameter, amount, number of additions, and remaining time.
children.title: Parameters and Skills

children.content:
Store and inventory

The store is divided into items, potions and rewards. Product availability varies by tier; the card shows price, description, effect and quantity limits.

  • Select the product, quantity and click “Buy”. If there are not enough coins, a credit for the missing amount may be offered for an authorized product from level 3.
  • The prices of most built-in products rise with inflation. Some items have stock limits or are one-of-a-kind items.
  • Inventory can be filtered by type; the selected type is saved for the new interface. The consumable item is used with the “Use” button; The permanent effect of the equipment lasts as long as the item is in the inventory.
  • Allowed items are sold for 75% of the current price. Quest rewards and some unique items cannot be sold.
  • “Freeze” is used through a separate selection of a suitable project or global streak.
  • The lottery ticket opens a separate “5 out of 30” drawing window: the numbers appear in order, matches are highlighted in green, and mismatches are highlighted in red. The prize is awarded after the drawing is completed and depends on two or more matching numbers.

In the rewards store, you can create a personal reward: set the name, price and inflation effect. It does not provide a gaming effect - purchase and use serve as a promise of real reward. Personal rewards can be changed and deleted.
children.title: Shop and inventory

children.content:
Quests, buffs, and debuffs

Quests unlock by level and are divided into available, active, and completed.

  1. Select an available quest, read the condition and reward, and click "Take Quest."
  2. Fulfill the condition in projects or game mode. The app periodically checks only active quests and automatically completes those that meet the requirements.
  3. You can decline an active quest: it will return to the available list and lose the dates of the current attempt.

The reward may include coins, experience, items, and buffs. A completed quest remains in the history and cannot be repeated.

Buffs increase stats, debuffs decrease them. The effect card shows the source, change coefficient, magnitude, and duration. Temporary effects disappear after expiration; compatible stackable effects show the quantity and total.
children.title: Quests, buffs, and debuffs

children.content:
Bank

The bank is opened with a button in the character block. It shows your credit score, limit, daily rates and estimated income. The rating depends on the level, expected income from text and streaks, property, deposits and credit history.

  • Credit Available from level 3, only one at a time and within the limit. The first payment is due the next day. If the balance is sufficient, the daily payment is debited automatically; Manual, partial and full payment are also available.
  • A missed payment after the end of the day adds a penalty of 1.5% of the balance, but not less than 5 coins, causes 10 damage and worsens the rating.
  • Contribution debits the selected amount and capitalizes the interest daily. It can be replenished. The option with withdrawal of accumulated interest allows you to withdraw it once a day; refusing this opportunity ups the ante.
  • Closing the deposit early returns the principal amount, but burns the interest. After the deadline, the principal amount and remaining income are returned.

There can be one loan and one deposit at the same time. Banking events are also saved in the Notifications center: you can read them one at a time or mark them all at once without losing your history.
children.title: Bank

content:
Game mode

Game mode turns actual writing into character development. It is enabled in the settings and takes into account positive entries from regular projects and synchronized sources.

Coins and experience are awarded for text, lines, completion of projects, tests, sessions and manuscript milestones. Coins are spent in the store and bank, experience levels up, and inspiration controls the Creative Rhythm functions.

Game data is saved separately from projects. Disabling the mode hides the tab, but does not delete the character, inventory or achievements.
title: Game mode

children.content:
Inspiration and abilities

1 inspiration is awarded for every 500 characters added. It is also given for successful sessions, challenges, milestones, and certain items. The maximum is 100; relics can increase the actual award.

The current reserve passively increases text rewards from 0% to 10%. Inspiration can be spent on one of the pending effects:

  • Creative Impulse — 30: +25% coins and experience for the next positive entry.
  • Session Spark — 25: +25% to the next successful writing session.
  • Challenge Focus — 40: +25% to the next completed daily or weekly challenge.

The same effect cannot be activated a second time while it is pending application. The session bonus is not spent on failure, while focus is until the actual completion of the trial.
children.title: Inspiration and abilities

children.content:
Daily in-game goal

At the beginning of each writing day, three sentences of different types and complexities are created. The first is selected automatically; the other can be chosen before completion for 15 inspiration.

  • Daily volume: write the specified number of characters. The base is 80% of the average result of productive days over the previous 14 days, rounded to the nearest hundred and limited to the range of 500–5,000. If there is no story, the base is 1,000.
  • Session rhythm: complete 1–3 successful writing sessions.
  • Editor’s day: complete 1–2 successful sessions with the intention “Edit text”.

Difficulty “Easy”, “Normal”, or “Hard” changes the goal and reward. After completion, coins, experience, and 10 inspiration points are awarded. “Challenge Focus,” the Explorer bonus, and relics increase coins and experience.

Completed goals cannot be changed. A new day creates a new set and resets unfinished progress. The “new goal token” switches to the next option for free.

Do not confuse: this is a game challenge, not a cumulative project goal by deadline.
children.title: Daily Game Challenge

children.content:
Weekly challenges

Select one challenge for the current week:

  • Marathon: 10,000 characters; reward 500 coins and 1,500 XP.
  • Rhythm: positive entries on 4 different days; 400 coins and 1,200 XP.
  • Clean Flow: 5 successful writing sessions; 450 coins and 1,350 XP.
  • Editorial Week: 3 successful sessions with the intent to edit; 425 coins and 1,300 experience.

Upon completion, an additional 20 inspiration is awarded. 'Trial Focus', the Researcher specialization, and relics multiply coins and experience.

In the usual way, the selected trial does not change and remains until next Monday, even after completion. The active skill of the Researcher replaces it with the next option but resets progress. With the start of a new week, the old trial is removed.
children.title: Weekly challenges

children.content:
Writing sessions

Select a mode, intention, duration of 15, 25, 45 or 60 minutes and a positive goal in symbols. In a regular session, only added text increases progress. If the Edit Text intent is selected, the absolute change in total volume is taken into account: writing +500 or −500 will add 500 characters processed.

  • Sprint: only 15 minutes, +15% reward.
  • Stream: free mode without an additional multiplier.
  • Deep work: only 45 or 60 minutes, +25%.
  • Editorial pass: requires "Edit Text" intent, +20%.

The application determines the editorial volume by the difference between the previous and new totals. Rewording text without changing the overall scope is not automatically detected and does not create a progress record.

Click “Finish” to record the result: bronze - 100% of the goal, silver - 125%, gold - 150%. Success gives a base of 25 coins with inflation, 250 experience and 10 inspiration, then mode, rank, streak, specialization and other bonuses are applied. Silver or gold completed before the end of the timer receives another +10%.

Failure does not give a reward and resets the streak if it is not protected. Cancellation is not considered a result and does not affect the streak. When the timer expires, the session ends automatically, even if another tab is open; After closing the application, the result will be recorded the next time it is launched.

Each successive success adds +3% to the reward, up to a maximum of +15%. The last 20 results are stored; a short history is available in the status tooltip.
children.title: Writing sessions

children.content:
Specializations and mastery

Specializations open at level 3. Once selected, you can change direction only after 14 days. The passive bonus increases by 2.5 percentage points for each new skill rank; Ranks are achieved at 0, 3, 8, 15 and 25 mastery experience.

  • Marathon runner: from +15% for entries of at least 3,000 characters; such a recording gives the experience of mastery.
  • Ritualist: from +25% for successful sessions; Every success provides mastery experience.
  • Finisher: from +20% for completing sources and projects; Mastery comes from milestones and completions.
  • Researcher: from +20% for daily and weekly trials; completed challenges grant mastery.
  • Editor: from +25% for successful sessions with the intent to edit; They also develop skills.

"Textbook of Mastery" adds 2 experience for the current specialization. Experience from different specializations is stored separately and retained after a shift.
children.title: Specializations and Mastery

children.content:
Active specialization skills

A skill can be activated once every 24 hours. The pending effect remains until the appropriate event occurs; new use is unavailable until then.

  • Long Breath: +30% to the next entry of at least 3,000 characters.
  • Ritual Power: +30% to the next successful session; if the next completed session fails, instead of the bonus, it preserves the streak once.
  • Rush to the Finale: +30% to the next new milestones of a manuscript, reached by a single entry.
  • New Route: Immediately replaces the active unfinished weekly challenge with the next one and resets its progress.
  • Precise Gaze: +30% to the next successful editor session.

The recovery countdown begins only after successful activation. An unsuitable record or session does not consume the pending effect.
children.title: Active specialization skills

children.content:
Creative events

Each individual positive entry of at least 1,000 characters is considered a productive action. After five such actions, one pending event appears. Until it is resolved, nothing new is created.

When an event is pending, select an option from the list and click Resolve Event. “Safe Choice” always gives the specified reward, while “Take a Risk” offers an increased reward with a 55% chance of success. The exact outcome of the selected option is shown in a tooltip.

  • Unexpected idea: guaranteed 6 inspirations; risk - 15 inspiration or loss 5.
  • Second Wind: guaranteed +10% to the next entry; risk - +30% or loss of 8 inspiration.
  • Lucky Find: guaranteed 50 coins; risk - 150 coins or nothing.

The event does not open the modal window while writing text. It waits for a decision on the “Creative Rhythm” tab, is applied exactly once and then goes into the history of the last 20 events.
children.title: Creative Events

children.content:
Manuscript path

The final project or source receives one-time rewards for achieving milestones for the first time. If one entry has jumped several boundaries, all missing rewards are given:

  • 10% “Spark of Design”: 25 coins, 250 experience, 2 inspiration.
  • 25% “First chapters”: 50 coins, 500 experience, 3 inspiration.
  • 50% "Tipping Point": 100 coins, 1,000 experience, 5 inspiration.
  • 75% “Finish Line”: 150 coins, 1,500 experience, 7 inspiration.
  • 90% “Almost done”: 200 coins, 2,000 experience, 8 inspiration.
  • 100% “Manuscript Complete”: 300 coins, 3,000 experience, 10 inspiration.

Coins scale with inflation; Specialization, items and relics can multiply coins and experience. The path of each source is stored separately. Renaming transfers the achieved milestones to the new name, so there is no repeat award. An endless project has no boundaries.
children.title: Manuscript path

children.content:
Cabinet, relics and kits

The Cabinet is located on the right side of the game mode, on the “Cabinet” tab next to the “Inventory” tab.

Relics are opened automatically along the boundaries of different manuscripts. A locked relic hides the name and description, but shows the condition and progress.

  • 10% of one text: “Ink Candle”, +1% per written text.
  • 50% of one text: “Map of plot twists”, +3% for tests.
  • 100% of one text: “Binding of the first manuscript”, +5% for completions.
  • 25% of three texts: “First Chapter Shelf”, +3% for successful sessions.
  • 75% of one text: “Tipping Point Pen”, +5% abroad.
  • 90% of one text: “Finish line lamp”, +10% to inspiration received.
  • 50% of three texts: “Atlas of Three Worlds”, +2% for written text.
  • 100% of three texts: “Shelf of completed manuscripts”, +10% for completions.

The “Path of the Great Manuscript” set of five relics of one full path adds +3% to all coins and experience rewards. An “Author's Library” of three multi-project relics increases inspiration received by 20%. The effects of relics and open sets stack.
children.title: Cabinet, Relics, and Sets

children.content:
Items of creative rhythm

  • Potions and sparks of inspiration restore the specified supply up to the maximum.
  • Inkwell of the flow adds +25% to the next successful session; the effect remains upon failure.
  • Manuscript compass adds +25% to the next new milestones achieved by a single entry.
  • Mastery tutorial gives 2 experience to the selected specialization.
  • New goal token chooses the next option of an as-yet-uncompleted daily game goal for free.
  • Ritual thread saves a series once during an unsuccessful completed session; up to three defenses can be prepared.
  • Quality Medal increases the next successful bronze or silver session by one rank; only one can be prepared at a time.

The item is written off only after successful use. If the condition is currently unattainable or the effect limit has been reached, it remains in the inventory.
children.title: Creative Rhythm Items

content:
Creative Rhythm

"Creative Rhythm" is a large set of motivational mechanics within the game mode: inspiration, daily game goal, weekly challenge, writing sessions, specialization, creative events, and the manuscript path.

All mechanics progress with real application events. Symbolic goals receive only the positive difference of a new entry; session goals—only a successfully completed session; editorial goals—a successful session with the intention "Edit text." In such a session, progress is the absolute change in length: both additions and reductions count.

State is saved between launches. Daily prompts change with the new writing day, the weekly challenge changes on Monday, and an active writing session continues to count real time even when the application is closed.
title: Creative rhythm

content:
Settings and project stages in the cloud

In the cloud settings, check the settings of the connected project. Confirm support on all devices and enable settings synchronization. The initial publication is performed only by your action.

If the versions are different, use the cloud one, save the local one as a new change, or edit the result. If there is a conflict, choose an option or make a general result. All previous versions are retained. Once approved, regular editing creates encrypted changes. An unfinished activity can be safely continued.

When importing, the verified cloud history sets the project parameters; conflict requires choice. Without such a history, a local title and separate confirmation of publication are required. Local paths, documents and covers are saved on the device.

The long cloud story is read in parts. If the import asks to continue, repeat the import: the scanned pages are saved even after a restart. If the safe volume is exceeded, the history is saved, but import is blocked. If a new option appears during reconciliation, the old solution does not select the winner: check all current versions and create a new solution.

The stages of a connected project are published only after the explicit action “Submit stages of this device” and the settings have been agreed upon. The order is sent after the stages are confirmed. Normal step and order changes are saved before submission and are displayed after verified confirmation. If there is a conflict, choose the cloud option or save the local result; a new option requires reselection. "Safe to Continue" resumes after restart. Selected deletion preserves child data: physical deletion and deordering remain blocked until they are fully verified.

Folders, placement and the order of connected projects can sync between devices. In cloud settings, click “Check project structure”, then explicitly choose “Publish project structure”. Local projects, their positions and folder membership stay on this device and are not connected to the cloud. A folder can contain both local and connected projects. If changes happen at the same time, choose a final version; saved versions are retained. Deleting a folder does not delete projects or remove their placement: first explicitly move projects or remove them from the folder. An unfinished publication can safely continue after a restart.
title: Settings and project stages in the cloud

content:
Project and stage notes in the cloud

Publish plain project notes and stage notes separately using “Publish notes” in cloud settings. All registered devices in the account must confirm support for this format before publication. After verified confirmation, ordinary editing and deletion create encrypted changes. HTML project notes retain their existing cloud history. Mind-map notes are published with their maps using the separate “Publish maps” action. Stage notes require an agreed, live stage; deleting a stage does not delete its notes. Conflicts preserve both versions: review the text and explicitly choose a version. If data changes during your choice, refresh the state and choose again. Sending without a response can safely be retried after restarting.
title: Project and stage notes in the cloud

content:
Reading cloud documents on Web

Sign in to your cloud account, unlock the key with your encryption password and open a project from the cloud list. Click “Open project for reading”, then select a document in “Documents”.

This mode displays the text of a project document without a stage. After changing the text on Desktop, click “Open project for reading” to receive the verified next revision. The selected document stays open. Formatting and browser editing are not supported yet. Unsupported or damaged history is refused. A server connection is required. Sign in and unlock the key again after restarting. Locking the key hides the open text.
title: Reading cloud documents on Web

content:
Diagnosis and problem reporting

In the desktop app, go to Settings → Diagnostics. The log helps you find the cause of the error and is stored only on this computer, including after a restart. The texts of documents and notes, names, passwords, keys and login data are not recorded in it. There is no automatic sending.

  1. Click Clear Log.
  2. Repeat the action that is causing the problem.
  3. Return to Diagnostics and click Copy Log or Export Log.
  4. Paste the result into a message for verification or attach the selected JSONL file.

The last 512 events are stored, with a maximum of 512 KB of content. Up to 100 latest events are copied, no more than 60 KB, with a mark for reduction. Export saves all available log. Clearing only deletes the diagnostic log.

In the status cards, the “Technical Information” section shows the code and number of the request. They help you associate the error with activity in the log. For the streak recovery issue, repeat the recovery in developer mode after clearing the log and submit the result for verification.
title: Diagnostics and reporting a problem

content:
Keyboard shortcuts

  • Ctrl+N / Command+N: open project creation.
  • Ctrl+H / Command+H: open Help.
  • Ctrl+S / Command+S: open synchronization for the selected project or stage.
  • Ctrl+E / Command+E: edit the selected project or stage.
  • Delete: delete the selected project or stage after confirmation.
  • Ctrl+Shift+S / Command+Shift+S: go to statistics.
  • Ctrl+Shift+C / Command+Shift+C: complete the selected project or stage.
  • Ctrl+Shift+H / Command+Shift+H: archive the selected project.

In Help, Ctrl+F or Command+F moves focus to search. Shortcuts are not intercepted while typing in a field, editor, or drop-down list.

All interactive elements are available from the keyboard in the normal Tab order. Enter or Space activates the selected button, and Escape closes supported dialogs and menus.
title: Hotkeys

content:
Project and stage maps in the cloud

Choose “Publish maps” in cloud settings for a connected project. Opening a project, signing in and synchronizing do not publish maps automatically. All registered devices must support maps. Project maps and each stage map have separate histories. Linked note text, title, checklist, tags, color, pinning, archive and order travel with the map. Ordinary notes retain their separate history. A combined map is a view of separate maps: refresh before saving if any displayed version changes. Conflicts preserve complete map and note versions; review them and choose a version. Another device’s local map is preserved until an explicit choice. An unresolved or deleted stage blocks map application. Unsupported extensions are not published. A saved upload can safely be retried after restarting.
title: Project and stage maps in the cloud

content:
Project and milestone documents in the cloud

In the cloud settings, select “Publish documents” for the connected project. Opening a project and normal synchronization does not publish previous documents. All registered devices must support this format. Once published, regular saves transfer the complete document: title, text, and area of ​​the project or step.

"Move Document" changes the scope within the same project and preserves the history. There must be no other document in the selected area, and the step must be consistent and not deleted. Transferring to another project is not supported. In case of competing changes, the full versions are preserved; review the text and select the result along with the title and area. If new versions become available, please select again.

Word and Scrivener files are linked separately on each device. First, save the new document in the editor. The path and binding are not sent to the cloud. Accepting Word's changes requires you to take action and check the file again. Deleting a document preserves your cloud history and does not delete the external file. Recording of progress remains local.

Additional unsupported data and unresolved previous migration records are stored on the device and block publication. This version does not transfer such lossy data. If the stage is unavailable or deleted, receipt of the document awaits verification; subsequent events do not allow confirmation of the missed event. Incomplete submissions are safely retried after restart.
title: Project and milestone documents in the cloud

content:
Cloud progress history

For a connected project, open cloud settings and click “Publish progress”. Signing in, opening a project and background synchronization do not publish history automatically. All registered devices must support this format; update older devices.

Each entry preserves a historical action, its delta, absolute resulting total and preceding history. Projects with stages have a separate history for each stage. Totals, percentages, remaining amounts and statistics are recalculated from the selected history and current project settings.

Simultaneous entries on two devices are preserved as separate branches and are not added automatically. Choose the history to keep or explicitly rebase the other branch’s actions in the displayed order. The result is shown before confirmation. The other history and original actions remain preserved.

Correcting or deleting an old entry requires explicit rebasing of later dependent actions. If the history changes while choosing, review it again. Inconsistent old entries block publication and remain on the device.

The writing day is preserved with the action. Changing the project unit changes the display while retaining the original historical facts. Progress synchronization does not synchronize the game: receiving an entry from another device neither repeats rewards nor starts a new game action.
title: Cloud progress history

content:
Game progress synchronization

In cloud settings, click “Publish game progress”. Publication is explicit: login, opening the game and background synchronization do not migrate previous state automatically. All registered devices must support game history. Previous rewards, balances and items are transferred without paying rewards again; local projects are not connected automatically.

Supported new game actions are preserved together with project and account history. Receiving progress alone does not grant a reward. Retries and restarts do not create another reward. Data remains preserved while waiting for source history. Unsupported extensions and developer mode changes block publication and remain local.

If game histories diverge, choose a preserved history. All branches remain in the history; review your choice again if new changes arrive. Restoring the game projection uses authenticated history but does not remove other migration restrictions. Deleting a progress entry does not revoke a reward automatically. To reverse a reward explicitly, select it and confirm a separate action; the original reward remains preserved.
title: Game progress synchronization

content:
Encrypted project covers

After enabling cloud project settings, an existing cover remains local. Choose “Publish cover” in cloud settings. Every registered device must support this feature. Starting the application, signing in or opening a project does not publish a cover.

The cover is encrypted before upload: the server cannot see the image. After the first confirmed publication, ordinary replacement and removal create encrypted changes to project settings. A local project’s cover stays only on the device.

If an encrypted cover is unavailable or fails verification, the verified image is preserved while complete synchronization is temporarily delayed. Retry later; unfinished publication and waiting for a cover survive restart.

For concurrent replacement, removal or changes to other settings, choose a complete project version in the existing conflict section. You can preview each version’s verified cover. Removing a cover does not erase historical encrypted images on the server.
title: Encrypted project covers

content:
Local files on each device

Word and Scrivener are attached separately on each device. Paths, selected sources and local checks are not synchronized.

Export a Word copy first or reattach an existing file. Selecting an existing file compares content without overwriting it. If versions differ, explicitly import Word or write the WORTA version; you can export a separate copy. Compare again if WORTA or the file changed since comparison.

A missing local file does not delete cloud text or progress. Choose another path explicitly. Word/Scrivener progress changes require confirmation of the comparison. Local links are unavailable on Web; WORTA text remains available.
title: Local files on each device
